title: Contextual Role Scopes: Inline Preview for Workspace & Org RBAC
creator: Avery Collins
description:
Problem: Admins and platform engineers frequently need to understand the immediate effect of a role change across both workspace and org contexts without leaving the role editor. Current flows require multiple pages: role list -> role detail -> separate access review or who-can query, which breaks context and increases approval friction. Goal: design an inline contextual preview and compact timeline that surfaces the effective scope (workspaces, projects, API keys) and recent audit events when editing or creating roles. This reduces accidental over-privilege and speeds up reviews.

Proposed solution overview: Inline Role Scope Preview is an accordion panel inside the role editor that contains three compact lenses: 1) Scope Summary (who will be affected, count of users/groups/service principals), 2) Quick Impact Tiles (Top 5 affected workspaces or highest-risk principals), 3) Recent Access Timeline (last 7 days of grant/revoke events + source). The panel supports a live "What-If" toggle that runs a simulated evaluation against a cached permission graph (backend) and shows added/removed principals and a risk indicator. The UI is designed to fit both org-level and workspace-level role editors, with localized copy and condensed view for narrow screens.

Design constraints and trade-offs: 1) Live evaluation vs cached snapshot: live is accurate but can be slow; we propose a cached snapshot with a button to re-run evaluation for authoritative results. 2) Detail density vs legibility: prioritize succinct counts and 1-click drilldown to full access-review screen. 3) Security considerations: preview must not leak membership details beyond the viewer's permissions; we rely on existing console permission checks and redact principal names when the viewer lacks visibility. 4) Performance: preview must not block save; it is advisory and snapshots are updated asynchronously.

Screens & states: - Role editor (collapsed) -> shows small badge "Preview available" - Inline panel collapsed/expanded - What-If running state with spinner and early results - Snapshot stale warning with timestamp and "Refresh" CTA - Empty-state when no principals are affected - Redacted state for limited-viewers - Error state (evaluation failed) with retry and contact link

Accessibility: keyboard focusable accordion, readable color contrast for risk indicators, screen-reader labels for tiles and timeline entries.

Metrics to validate success: reduce number of role edit follow-ups from security reviewers by 30% within first 6 weeks; decrease time-to-approval for role edits by 20%; adoption: 40% of role edits open the preview before saving.

Next steps: prototype in Figma, run moderated usability tests with 4 customers and internal SRE/Legal, handoff to Eng for API contract and performance SLAs, and prepare release notes and admin training material.
comments: 2025-02-21: Initial whiteboard session with PM (Elena Park) and Eng (Samir Desai). Captured primary use cases and constraints.
2025-02-24: Low-fidelity frames created; validated compact tiles approach with two engineers. Concern raised about expensive permission queries for orgs with >10k principals.
2025-02-28: Decided to implement cached snapshot + on-demand re-eval to avoid save latency. Added stale-warning state to design.
2025-03-03: Accessibility review meeting — confirmed keyboard + screen reader flows; adjusted color for risk heatmap.
2025-03-05: Design review with Security and Privacy — agreed redaction rules and logging requirements. Marked 'In Review' and requested FE/BE feasibility estimates from ENG.

acceptance_criteria: Inline preview panel visible in role editor for org and workspace roles when user has permission to view access summaries.
What-If toggle runs cached evaluation and shows delta between current and proposed role assignments.
Snapshot shows counts of affected principals, top 5 affected workspaces, and up to 7 days of recent access events.
Panel includes 'Refresh' CTA to force authoritative re-eval and handles failure gracefully.
All UI states accessible by keyboard and labeled for screen readers.
Backend APIs documented and provided by ENG with acceptable latency for cached responses (<300ms) and explicit contract for on-demand re-eval.
Security review sign-off confirming redaction rules and audit logging is in place.
decision_log: 2025-02-24: Use cached snapshot as default for performance reasons (agreed by Eng).
2025-02-28: Add 'Refresh' CTA to re-run authoritative evaluation on demand.
2025-03-05: Security approved redaction behavior: show counts to low-privilege viewers, show names only to those with membership visibility.
